reviews.text: Visited M50 in the late morning and enjoyed exploring the mix of contemporary galleries and studios. It’s a great spot for discovering local artists and creative work, with plenty of variety as you wander. Some spaces felt a bit quiet or hit-and-miss, but overall it’s an interesting and easy stop for art lovers.
Beautiful space with lots of art galleries, (vintage) shops & food/drinks. I enjoyed this a lot and hope to come back, excellent art.
Interesting art district to spend up to 3 hours. Most galleries open by 11am. There are a few cafes and coffee shops to get a snack. Island 6 and Pearlota were my favorite places I stopped at.
M50 It's known for its stunning art galleries, trendy boutiques, and street art.

Inspiring and chill area with lots of nice galleries and cafes. The art had a good variety and there are some nice shops as well. Nice place to see a more industrial gritty space converted into art walk.

We first visited this over 15 years ago, when it opened. Then, it was just a budding place for artists, with small studios dotted about. Today, it had grown into several buildings, with large galleries and experimental spaces. It was good to see that artists are still around, though these seem to now be of younger age, and more into experimental art. There is even a lifestyle store, selling quite unique and quaint 'period' furniture, and even offering coffee on the terrace. There are also a number of small cafes, as well as a couple of restaurants.

“Art enclave of shanghai” M50 is one of the famous contemporary art zones of Shanghai. The place was actually a mill producing clothes, which was later converted into a place to display art. Talking about the place, it has more than 100 art cafes with free entrance; the walls are all painted with different designs, art forms and graphics. The main aim of the artists is to display their art and to sell as much as possible. Apart from paintings you can also find photo studios, fashion designers, etc. I could see lot of foreigners here more than the locals as this place is quite famous among the foreigners. If you are an art lover like me then this place is not to be missed.
Visited at Kate evening so could not visit any gallery or shop but it was still very nice to stroll around.

Here’s when to come here, when it’s your second or third time to Shanghai OR if you’re big into art. Great galleries of local artists and a cool hipster space. A couple of ok cafes. Glad I visited but I only need to see it once.

A very different art center, utilizing the old factory. Unlike the many other tourisy old town places, there was no crowds. Displaying various artists' work and their studios You can enjoy a quiet, leisure afternoon going thru the studio and maybe see how east met/mix west!

For artists and art lovers, M50 district might be their must visit destination. It is considered as a creativity and art hub in Shanghai. 👨‍🎨👩‍🎨 You can walk through different studios and galleries enjoying the creations and unique works 🎨🎭

M50 (莫干山路50号) is an industrial look/warehouse turned into art district kind of place. It's free to the public and if you're a creative person/art enthusiast or even if you just want to check a cool open space with lots of galleries, studios, cafes and anything art related. Architects and photographers will have a good time visiting this place. There are countless alleys to discover, maybe one visit won't be enough, so come with time to walk around and seat down for a coffee and talk with your friends.

I love this place so much. It’s an area is for a creative people. It quite hard to go because it’s not nearby the station but finally I’m here. There are many points in each area for taking photo. I will really appreciated if this area have more restaurants or café for hopping.

Don’t visit this place during public holidays, most stores & galleries are closed. A small space for arts and creatives and there were a few cafes in this area. 10 minutes walk to the metro station, Jiang Ning Road (Line 1).

A true gem of Shanghai. The art galleries are a great place to walk around and take in some of the local expression. The galleries are staffed with friendly and knowledgeable individuals who will gladly explain to you the local art culture. They often have live music and great food!!
Awesome place with too many shops for artistic items and decor. Should definitely visit when in Shanghai.

Conserved industrial buildings that are converted into art spaces and galleries. Interesting facts about the building provided near building entrances. Many free galleries to wander in and out of. Worthy of a half day exploration.
Great place which has lots of studios for free entry. Various artful works that can spend at least couple hours. Most not allowed photo.
Great place for art and good coffee although some coffee shops have unclear opening hours. Feels more like London or Berlin than China but if you're into that it's worth a visit.
Amazing exhibits, a must see (non tourist) place in Shanghai. Free admission, not crowded (as every other place in Shanghai) and also hidden artistic gems in every corner of this place. 10/10 Mao's

Nestled in a repurposed industrial area, M50 is a sprawling collection of mostly free galleries and studios that showcase the locals youth culture. it’s a unique and authentic slice of the city’s creative culture. The vibe here is gritty yet inspiring, concealing the locals artist’s take on various issues: education system, capitalism etc. Highly recommend for anyone who wants to explore a slice of art, creativity, urban exploration.

This converted textile mill retains original Stalinist-era concrete, its pockmarks from old machinery now framing avant-garde installations. The smell of oil paint mixes with latent cotton fibers in the air. Artists intentionally leave windows grimy to diffuse northern light—a trick borrowed from 19th-century ateliers. Graffiti on the west wall changes weekly, documenting the city’s subconscious in spray paint.

Lovely contemporary art district. I preferred it to 798 in Beijing. Artworks were funny, moving, unusual, and executed with great imagination and technical skill. My favorite were some photos of sculptures created to call attention to the lack of access to education for children of migrant workers. A book was encased in barbed wire, or surrounded by shards of glass.
Be mesmerized by amazing artwork and spend time with Shanghai's top artists at M50.
A fantastic space and make sure you look at the 1000 Trees shopping centre next door. Love the art community in M50. Quite a lot closed on Mondays, but still fun. For art lovers.

Nice little village of art studios and galleries in industrial buildings. I believe that a real art connaisseur could spend lots of time there, however, I would not recommend this place to any "simple tourists", unless you are looking for some unique, handmade souvenir. The shops are actually nice, but there were also so many places going under construction that there was not much left of the atmosphere because of all the trucks and construction worker going around. Oh, and go there when the weather is good! The little cafés look promising!

Good place to visit for a day out. Not very touristy, so there's not all that many people around, which is great. There's plenty of galleries to wander around and look at and/or buy artwork. As others have mentioned the food and drink here is mediocre at best so perhaps eat and drink elsewhere before coming. Entry is free!
Cozy space for artwork and creativity. Had a great time spending with a nice restaurant also.

There are some cool galleries and exhibits here but a lot of the galleries weren't open. This is not as cool as the 798 district in Beijing but def interesting if you are into art. My friend found and bought a REALLY great painting here and the artist was there working. So that was DEF a great thing. Eat before you come. Not a lot of good food options here.

M50 is so charming. This review is a bit unfair as I went during mid-autumn festival and everything is mostly shut, but some art studios and shops were open. Most don't allow photography and a minority require tickets. A majority have shops attached to them, and a few are outright selling the exhibited works for staggering costs. For the casual buyer, there are options, but in terms of art collecting, this one is for clientele with deep pockets.
Really cool creative space with loads of really good galleries. I even bought a piece of art from the artist themselves! Has some places to eat and get a drink so good place to spend an afternoon.

À Pékin il y a l’espace 798. À Shanghai, c’est le M50. Même principe, en plus petit. Mais tout aussi sympathique! Des petites rues charmantes et calmes, des installations artistiques, des galeries d’art, des boutiques de poteries fait main (parfait si vous voulez ramener de magnifiques services à thé, uniques, et pas si chers!). Quelques cafés où il est bon de se détendre à quelques minutes aussi! Bref, un coin tranquille, parfait pour se détendre!

很棒的老工廠再生藝術園區 同為文青來訪著名景點，相較於田子坊、新天地的濃厚商業氣息，這裡大多有的是純粹的藝術，錯綜複雜的動線布局初訪時看似困擾，走久了才發現這其實也是種巧思，盡管發揮好奇心去小巷、小樓梯間探險吧！在這裡不管是看似死路的轉角、看似禁入的二樓、不起眼的後巷，藝術總是會突然不期而遇，這就是所謂柳暗花明又一村的驚奇感吧？ 我覺得這裡不管是打卡拍照走馬看花、抑或要來場文藝青年的深度文化之旅，都能輕易消磨掉上海行的一個下午，並讓人有內心滿載而歸的充實感，來上海除了有名的外灘豫園外，行程時間有餘之際來這晃晃也是不錯的。

상해여행에서 가장 좋았던 곳 중 하나였다. 젊은 아티스트들과 예술가들이 모인 곳이라고 해서 갔는데 소소한 전시들도 많았고 곳곳에서 자유분방함이 느껴졌다. 마치 우리나라로 따지면 성수동, 홍대 같은 느낌 ...? 예술쪽으로 상하이가 뜨고 있다는 얘기는 들었지만 와닿지 않았었는데 전시들을 보면서 왜 그런 얘기들이 나오는지 알 수 있었다. 중국에 갖고 있던 편견 하나를 부수는 경험이었다.
